newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Philippines agrees to back Taiwan's WTO bid.
newsitem.headline: Philippines agrees to back Taiwan's WTO bid.

text.p: The Philippines has signed a formal agreement with Taiwan to support the island's bid to join the World Trade Organisation, Taiwan's economics ministry said on Wednesday.
The agreement was signed at an economic cooperation forum between Taipei and Manila, a ministry statement said.
Taiwan has completed bilateral negotiations with 18 of the total 26 WTO member nations that sought such talks, but has signed formal agreements with only 14 countries, including the Philippines.
It still needs to complete talks with eight more members -- the United States, the European Union, Hong Kong, Canada, Singapore, Thailand, Switzerland and Argentina.
Taiwan applied in 1990 to join the WTO's predecessor, the General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade, as a customs territory under the name of Chinese Taipei.
GATT was replaced by the WTO in January 1995.
Taiwan has made major concessions in recent years as part of its drive to join the world trade body, allowing more imports, opening up domestic markets and dismantling state monopolies.
Taiwan has postponed its July target for joining the WTO to the end of 1997, although many analysts said the goal was too optimistic.
Rival China, which has regarded Taiwan as a renegade province since a civil war split them in 1949, has insisted it must join the WTO before Taiwan does.
